newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: PRESS DIGEST - CZECH REPUBLIC - JULY 16.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - CZECH REPUBLIC - JULY 16.

text.p: HOSPODARSKE NOVINY - The region of Hodonin was flooded yesterday. The number of deaths in northern Moravia is now 43, but many people are still missing. All affected districts received 13 million crowns from the cabinet for their initial expenses. The U.S. government announced yesterday that it will donate $100,000, and even Pope John Paul II expressed his concern.
- The European Commission of the EU yesterday approved humanitarian aid of 0.5 million ECU to eastern European countries affected by floods, and the Czech Republic will also recieve aid from UNESCO.
- For the first five months of this year, agricultural businesses increased sales by 1.1 percent in fixed prices, year-on-year. The number of employees, however, decreased by 5.7 percent.
- Tatra Koprivnice increased its half-year turnover, including that of its subsidiaries, by 77 percent, year-on-year, to 5.53 billion crowns.
- During the first half of this year, CKD Holding a.s. had consolidated gross profits of 300 million crowns. It plans this year to have gross profits of 597 million crowns.
MLADA FRONTA DNES - Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus announced yesterday that government bonds to help citizens in flooded areas will be available at commercial banks from the beginning of August.

- The Industry and Trade Ministry, which estimates flood damages under its authority at eight to 10 billion crowns, does not plan on a direct financial injection for damaged companies, but is preparing a number of measures to help them. The cabinet should decide today on aid to companies.

- The basic estimate of damages in the Agriculture Ministry is, according to Josef Lux, 12 billion crowns. Of this, more than six billion concerns farmers, and more than five billion represents damages to waterways and water equipment.
- During today's cabinet meeting, Agriculture Minister Josef Lux wants to propose that water payments for households increase due to damages caused by floods.
- Ceska Pojistovna has already registered nearly 3,000 insurance claims in flooded areas, although the number could climb to up to 100,000.
- The Czech National Bank yesterday decreased its weekly repo rate by 0.2 percentage points to 16 percent.

- The Regional Development Ministry has so far calculated that at least 1,173 houses and flats were damaged during the floods. At least 5,200 housing units were seriously damaged and about 2,080 families currently have no roofs over their heads.
PRAVO - Komercni Banka, Citibank and Atlantik Financni Trhy took the title as the best Czech financial institutions in their categories in the magazine Euromoney.

- Member countries of the World Trade Organisation agreed yesterday in Geneva that they will continue, during the week beginning September 22, to examine the Czech Republic's balance of payments and its justification for introducing an import deposit.
- Transport Minister Martin Riman and the general director of Czech Railways agreed to provide 12 freight trains daily to assure supplies for the four largest companies in Ostrava.

- Regional Development Minister Tomas Kvapil will propose today that citizens whose property was damaged in floods to the point where it is uninhabitable obtain 100-percent coverage from the government for damages.

- According to a poll from STEM, a record 31 percent of citizens would vote for the opposition Social Democratic Party in July (one percent more than in July), while 19.7 percent would vote for the Civic Democratic Party (ODS). The opposition would win if elections were held now.
LIDOVE NOVINY - The European Commission of the EU approved a proposal yesterday for six countries to enter the EU during the first wave, one of which is the Czech Republic.
- The cabinet agreed yesterday that while citizens currently pay an annual average of 800 crowns in cash for health care, in the future this amount should double to 1,600 crowns.
- President Vaclav Havel left for his holiday yesterday, which should last approximately one month. He and his wife will spend it within the Czech Republic.
-- Prague Newsroom, 420-2-2423-0003
